solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Married woman has caught a disease

indicators.note: something that has caught another thing holds it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A wife falls ill with some ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or ailment, a direct synonym for a disease.

clue.text: Poem written in 1050 for example

indicators.note: words written in a frame sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is 1000 and L is 50
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poem composed in the year 1050, cited as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The date 1050 looks like history but is just Roman numerals, M and L, with ODE written between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a pattern or specimen to be copied, which is what an example is.

clue.text: Dafter ladies or gents not so far away reportedly?

parts.note: the ladies and the gents are both a loo, a public toilet

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than written, so we keep its sound

parts.note: closer, that is nearer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the toilets are a silly distance away.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'nearer' ends with no R sound, so 'loo nearer' is heard as LOONIER. The ladies and gents are public toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Dafter means sillier or more crazy, which is what the comparative of loony means.

clue.text: Being stripped of individual recognition, deal with depression painfully

indicators.note: something done painfully is twisted and wrenched, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on coping with depression when one has lost one's sense of identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painfully' rearranges DEAL and DEPRESSION; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be depersonalised is to have one's individuality removed, to be treated as no one in particular.

clue.text: Wife involved in fall — there's some stuff stolen

indicators.note: a thing involved in another is caught up within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to sag is to drop or fall

explanation.surface: A wife caught up in a burglar's downfall, with loot on the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for a thief's booty, the goods taken in a robbery.

clue.text: Famous Scot tethers unruly brute — it may be found at side of house

definitions.text: it may be found at side of house

indicators.note: to tether is to tie in, so the Scot's name holds the other letters inside

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A well-known Scotsman ties up a wild animal beside his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges BRUTE as ERBUT, which WATT holds. A water butt is a large rain barrel fed by a downpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainwater barrel usually stands against an outside wall, catching water from the gutters.

clue.text: Chemical in body only egg can initially supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, bending freely, so the letters are bent into a new order
initially points to the opening letter of the word can

explanation.surface: Only an egg can at first provide some compound the body needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is an adverb (in a supple way): it rearranges ONLY, EGG and C, from 'can initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glycogen is the polysaccharide in which animals store glucose, mainly in liver and muscle.

clue.text: Pi is 'being in the spiritual realms' maybe

definitions.meaning: the mathematical constant pi is not the root of any polynomial with rational coefficients

explanation.surface: A claim that pi is otherworldly or mystical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' admits the mathematical sense is one of two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematicians call pi such a number, and the same word describes the mystical or supernatural.

clue.text: Bra-destroying feminist presumably wouldn't have this quarrel!

definitions.text: Bra-destroying feminist presumably wouldn't have this
definitions.meaning: having burnt her bra, she would have no support holding her chest high

explanation.surface: A joke about a bra-burning activist being spared a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part literally, as a bosom held up; the dashed form is the noun for a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust-up is a noisy argument or falling-out between people.

clue.text: Set produced by artist and fashion designer not right

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

indicators.note: not right means the letter R, for right, is dropped

parts.note: Christian Dior, the French couturier

explanation.surface: A painter and a couturier produce a stage set together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is a noun here, a receiving apparatus, not a stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio set is the receiver, so set alone can mean the wireless.

clue.text: Flowering plant got out of bed

definitions.meaning: a thorny shrub with fragrant blooms
got up in the morning, past tense of arise

explanation.definitionFit: The shrub with thorny stems shares its spelling with the past tense of rise.

clue.text: The usual question about the last bit of carpet needed for floor covering?

parts.note: par is the normal or expected level

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the question goes round the next letter

parts.note: a query is a question

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word carpet

explanation.surface: Someone asks the usual question about finishing off a carpet for the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquetry is inlaid wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern to make a floor.

clue.text: Ancient one has little hesitation interrupting boy: 'Don't give up!'

indicators.note: these pieces break into the boy's word, so they go inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
ancient means old
I is the Roman numeral one
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An old man stammers as he urges a lad to persevere.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going doggedly despite difficulty, an imperative of encouragement.

clue.text: Part of the body protected by gladiator sometimes

indicators.note: the letters are sheltered within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gladiator would sometimes guard part of his body with armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' signals the letters sit within 'gladiator sometimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Ecofriendly activity — i.e. with this making ice!

parts.note: C, the chemical symbol for ... by I and E gives the frozen water word

explanation.surface: An environmental process explained by its effect on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Carbon's symbol is C; let I.E. capture it and you get ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Capturing and storing carbon dioxide emissions is a green technology to slow climate change.

clue.text: Official register's showing bad man of star-like quality

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably
astral means of the stars

explanation.surface: A villain shows some celestial quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive, matching an adjective meaning of or for an official register.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadastre is a public record of land ownership, and this adjective describes such a survey.

clue.text: Led astray with fraud? That's terrible

indicators.note: gone astray means off course, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Being misled by deception is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges LED and FRAUD; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful and terrible are synonyms, both meaning very bad.

clue.text: Thinks tragedy could possibly be a sign of good things on the morrow?

definitions.text: a sign of good things on the morrow

indicators.note: signals that the letters might take another form when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mulls over a tragedy and wonders whether it bodes well for tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'Red sky at night, shepherd's delight', promising fine weather next day.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing sunset is proverbially a sign of fair weather on the following day.

clue.text: An enzyme one's found in unusual snake

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An enzyme turns up in a strange snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges SNAKE as KNASE, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinase is a class of enzyme that transfers phosphate groups to other molecules.

clue.text: Escape that sounds unlikely!

definitions.meaning: a flight from captivity or a crime scene
a cry of disbelief, like 'you're kidding!'

explanation.surface: A doubtful response to news of a breakout.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a fleeing, while the two-word cry expresses disbelief at something said.

clue.text: Friend of Sarah losing her head

indicators.note: the name loses its first letter

parts.note: Sally is a pet form of Sarah

explanation.surface: A friend of Sarah's who has lost control.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or friend who sides with you.

clue.text: Minister won't keep quiet — a serious offence

indicators.note: P, for piano or quiet, is dropped from the word

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A clergyman who refuses to be silent commits a grave crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a grave crime.

clue.text: In detail somehow without the first sign of contrast

definitions.text: In detail somehow without the first sign of contrast

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters surround the next one
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are put in a new order
points to the opening letter of the word contrast

explanation.surface: Things matching in every particular, with no hint of difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges IN DETAIL around C; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things the same in every detail show no contrast whatever, which is what matching means.

clue.text: Runner Steve's first sign of pain — due to this?

definitions.text: Runner Steve's first sign of pain — due to this?

parts.note: Steve Cram was a British middle-distance runner of the 1980s

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word pain

explanation.surface: An athlete's first twinge of pain, perhaps from a muscle spasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram was a famous British miler; the whole clue also suggests what a runner might suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful involuntary muscle contraction is a classic runner's affliction.

clue.text: Rope the man beginning to explore discovered in wooded area

indicators.note: found inside, so these letters go within the forest word

parts.note: a forest is a wooded area
he is the man

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word explore

explanation.surface: A man exploring a wood finds a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing boat a sheet is a rope controlling a sail, and this one serves the foresail.

clue.text: Cautious about minimal energy — when one's this?

definitions.text: Cautious about minimal energy — when one's this?

indicators.note: about means around, so the cautious word goes round the next letter

parts.note: wary means cautious

indicators.note: minimal means the least, so only the first letter of energy is used

explanation.surface: Being careful with one's dwindling strength when tired.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: with little energy one is tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Having very little energy left is what being tired or exhausted means.

clue.text: Attractive girl read French, getting a Second

indicators.note: a second copy is added, so the piece appears twice

parts.note: lu is the French past participle of lire, to read

explanation.surface: A pretty girl studied French and came away with a second-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Second' looks like a university degree class but means a second helping of the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is informal for something or someone remarkable, here a striking girl.

clue.text: Be awkward, as conceited young man that's put inside

indicators.note: inside means the put word goes within the young man's word

parts.note: a pup is an arrogant young fellow
to lay is to put down

explanation.surface: An arrogant youth being difficult after being locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To misbehave or cause trouble, as children or a faulty machine do.
